note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Grenada: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident deducts a personal allowance of XCD 36,000 and pays 10% on the first XCD 24,000 of taxable income and 28% above; residents are taxed on Grenada-derived income; there is no regional layer.
figures.applies: Individuals (183 days' presence makes a resident)

sources.said: The rate is 10% on the first XCD 24,000 and 28% on income exceeding this amount.
Deductions and allowances: A personal allowance of XCD 36,000 is granted.
Resident individuals are taxed on their income derived from Grenada. Nonresident individuals are taxed on income derived from or sourced in Grenada.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; returns are due by 31 March of the next year with the balance of tax.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year.
Tax returns must be filed by 31 March following the tax year, and the balance of tax is due upon the filing of the return.

figures.finding: National Insurance takes 6.25% of earnings from the employee and 7.25% from the employer, on earnings up to XCD 5,000 a month.

sources.said: Employers contribute at a rate of 7.25% and employees at a rate of 6.25% of an employee’s earnings. The contribution ceiling is XCD 5,000 per month.

figures.finding: Employers deduct income tax from salaries under PAYE; a business also pays a stamp tax on gross income (0% to XCD 36,000, 0.5% to 299,999, 0.7% from 300,000).

sources.said: A pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) system is used to deduct tax from the salaries of employees.

Stamp tax is paid on the gross income of a business as follows: • 0% on amounts up to and including XCD 36,000; • 0.5% on amounts in excess of XCD 36,000 up to and including XCD 299,999; and • 0.7% on amounts equal to or greater than XCD 300

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Grenada-sourced income; royalties, technical fees and certain other payments to a non-resident bear 15% withholding; the rule for a performer's fee and its finality were not found.

sources.said: Certain other payments to a nonresident company or individual may be subject to a 15% withholding tax rate, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: Royalties bear 15% withholding whether paid to a resident or a non-resident; no special regime for authors was found.

sources.said: Royalties paid to a resident or nonresident company or individual are subject to a 15% withholding tax rate, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: VAT is 15%; registration is required once supplies reach XCD 300,000 a year.

sources.said: Registration: The registration threshold is a total value of supplies of at least XCD 300,000 per annum.

sources.title: Deloitte, Grenada Highlights 2026
sources.said: The rate is 10% on the first XCD 24,000 and 28% on income exceeding this amount. … Deductions and allowances: A personal allowance of XCD 36,000 is granted. … Resident individuals are taxed on their income derived from Grenada. Nonresident individuals are taxed on income derived from or sourced in Grenada. … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … Tax returns must be filed by 31 March following the tax year, and the balance of tax is due upon the filing of the return. … Employers contribute at a rate of 7.25% and employees at a rate of 6.25% of an employee’s earnings. The contribution ceiling is XCD 5,000 per month. … A pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) system is used to deduct tax from the salaries of employees. … Stamp tax is paid on the gross income of a business as follows: • 0% on amounts up to and including XCD 36,000; • 0.5% on amounts in excess of XCD 36,000 up to and including XCD 299,999; and • 0.7% on amounts equal to or greater than XCD 300 … Certain other payments to a nonresident company or individual may be subject to a 15% withholding tax rate, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty. … Royalties paid to a resident or nonresident company or individual are subject to a 15% withholding tax rate, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty. … The standard rate is 15%. … Registration: The registration threshold is a total value of supplies of at least XCD 300,000 per annum.
